archived_note: Archived 2026-11-13 planning draft. Superseded by public/data/sites.json; not used by the app.
description: Curated lunar south-pole comparison sites for SelenoGrid. Coordinates identify representative points for Sun/Earth geometry, not certified landing ellipses.
selection_summary: Three sites were selected to separate the two main mission trade-offs: a near-pole site with near-continuous summer sunlight but a short Earth-visibility window, and two lower-latitude summit/plateau sites with longer Earth-visibility windows but regular solar night. Malapert Massif and Mons Mouton are at similar latitude but different longitude, so they also test whether a date shift changes the power/communications balance.
disclaimer: This dataset is a geometric, airless, topocentric approximation for comparison and education. It does not model terrain occlusion, LOLA horizon profiles, landing-ellipse safety, Earth phasing or link budget, or operational flight constraints. Do not use it for flight operations or a certified landing-site decision.

sites.name: Connecting Ridge
sites.region: Connecting Ridge candidate landing region, between Shackleton and Henson craters
sites.coordinate_source: Gracy & Lee (2024), LPSC 55, abstract 1695, "Candidate landing sites for Artemis 3 in two NASA candidate landing regions nearest the lunar South Pole": center of a 2 km-radius candidate landing site at 89.53432°S, 209.94767°E.
sites.coordinate_accuracy_note: Published representative point. The candidate landing site is a 2 km-radius circle, not a point; this coordinate is its published center.
sites.artemis_status: Proposed candidate site within the Connecting Ridge region from NASA's 2022 Artemis III candidate-region set. Connecting Ridge was not among the nine regions retained in NASA's October 2024 refinement.
sites.why_included: Near-pole endmember for the comparison. It is expected to maximize summer solar availability while showing how a near-pole site can still lose direct Earth line-of-sight for long intervals.
caveats: Representative point, not a certified landing ellipse.
Altitude is set to 0 km for the Horizons query; terrain elevation and local horizon occlusion are not modeled.
Connecting Ridge is not in NASA's refined 2024 list of nine Artemis III candidate regions; it is included as a well-documented near-pole comparison site.

sites.name: Malapert Massif
sites.region: Malapert Massif candidate landing region, lunar south polar highlands
sites.coordinate_source: Kring et al. (2025), JGR Planets, doi:10.1029/2024JE008905, citing the NASA-defined notional Artemis landing site at latitude 85.964°S, longitude 357.681°E near the summit of the Malapert massif.
sites.coordinate_accuracy_note: Published notional landing-site point used by NASA's Artemis III geology planning; the massif and candidate region extend well beyond this point.
sites.artemis_status: In NASA's refined 2024 list of nine Artemis III candidate landing regions (Malapert Massif).
sites.why_included: Trade-off site: a lower-latitude summit with long Earth-visibility windows, but a solar cycle that includes night during the January 2027 test window.
caveats: Representative point, not a certified landing ellipse.
Altitude is set to 0 km for the Horizons query; the massif's relief and local horizon are not modeled.
The coordinate is a notional NASA planning site, not a selected Artemis landing site.

sites.name: Mons Mouton
sites.region: Mons Mouton, near the western rim of Nobile crater, lunar south polar highlands
sites.coordinate_source: Meier et al. (2024), LPSC 55, abstract 2086, "Detailed geomorphologic analysis of lunar regions of interests": VIPER study Site 102 at 85.43°S, 31.73°E on Mons Mouton, near the western edge of Nobile crater.
sites.coordinate_accuracy_note: Published study-site point. It is representative of the Mons Mouton area, not a certified landing ellipse.
sites.artemis_status: In NASA's refined 2024 list of nine Artemis III candidate landing regions (Mons Mouton).
sites.why_included: Longitude contrast to Malapert Massif at similar latitude. The pair tests whether a date shift, rather than a latitude change, can improve the power/communications balance.
caveats: Representative point, not a certified landing ellipse.
Altitude is set to 0 km for the Horizons query; the plateau's relief and local horizon are not modeled.
The IAU center of Mons Mouton is 84.60°S, 31.00°E; the selected point is the published study site, not the feature center.
